general_requirements.text: Packaging material shall comply with the Packaging Regulations; where Indian Standards are unavailable, relevant international standards may be complied with.
Any material that comes or is likely to come into direct contact with food during packaging, preparation, storage, wrapping, transportation, sale or service shall be food grade.
Packaging shall be suitable for the product, storage conditions, filling/sealing equipment and transportation conditions.
Packaging shall withstand mechanical, chemical and thermal stresses encountered during normal transportation; flexible/semi-rigid containers may require overwrap.
Food shall be packed in clean, hygienic and tamper-proof packaging or containers.
Sealing material shall be compatible with the product, container and closure system.
Tin containers once used shall not be reused for packaging food.
Reused plastic containers of 5 L and above and reused glass bottles shall be suitably durable and easy to clean/disinfect.
Printing inks for food packages shall conform to IS 15495.
Printed surfaces of packaging material shall not come into direct contact with food.
Newspaper or similar material shall not be used for storing or wrapping food.
For multilayer packaging, food-contact or likely-food-contact layers shall meet the applicable Schedule I, II and III requirements.
Schedule I, II and III materials shall be compatible with intended use and shall not alter food quality or safety.
The FBO shall obtain a certificate of conformity from an NABL-accredited laboratory against these regulations for packaging that comes or is likely to come into direct contact with food.

checks: Free from visible specks, grease marks, cuts, pinholes and other blemishes.
Food-contact paper shall be food grade and free from contaminants.
Applicable Schedule I Indian Standard shall be met.
As far as possible free from blisters, mould marks, stones, chippings, cords, seeds and visible defects.
Smooth surface without cracks, pinholes or sharp edges.
Sealing surface free from hairline cracks and prominent seam marks.

prohibited_conditions: Copper or brass containers not properly tinned
checks: Use appropriate grades of metal/alloy where applicable.
Applicable Schedule II Indian Standard shall be met.

recycled_pet.condition: Only FCM-rPET complying with FSSAI-notified standards/guidelines and using FSSAI-approved recycling technology.
recycled_pet.guideline_source: Guidelines for acceptance of recycled PET as Food Contact Material (FCM-rPET), notified 23.05.2025

drinking_water_special_route.transparency_requirement: Colourless, transparent and tamper-proof; transparency not less than 85% light transmittance for listed bottle/container route, subject to the additional food-grade compatible-material proviso.
drinking_water_special_route.pigments_over_5l: Pigments/colorants conforming to IS 9833 may be allowed in ≥5 L polycarbonate and PET containers; transparency remains ≥85% for that route.
drinking_water_special_route.other_food_grade_materials_proviso: Other food-grade packaging materials compatible with the water may also be used; in such cases the transparency requirement does not apply.

schedule_i_paper_board.material: Vegetable parchment / grease proof paper / aluminium foil laminate

schedule_i_note: Wax used for coating paper/board shall be paraffin wax conforming to Type I of IS 4654.

schedule_iii_plastic.material: Flexible packaging materials for edible oils, ghee and vanaspati
HDPE materials for moulding and extrusion
Blow-moulded polyolefin containers >5 L to 60 L

categories.name: Pan Masala
materials: Paper, paperboard, cellulose or other naturally derived material free from plastic/synthetic polymers/laminates and free from aluminium foil/metallised layers
restrictions: No plastic, including PE, PP, polyester, PVC or other synthetic polymer/copolymer/laminate, in the naturally-derived-material route.
No aluminium foil or metallised layer in the naturally-derived-material route.
Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016 clauses 4(1)(f) and 4(1)(i) also apply.
